passages.section: The algebraic PCP theorem: a detailed account of the Lean proof
passages.quote: A polynomial-time verifier can check membership in any NP language by reading a constant number of bits from a suitably encoded proof. It uses only logarithmically many random bits, accepts a correct proof with certainty, and rejects every purported proof of a false statement with probability at least one half. This account explains the algebraic construction and the machine-level steps that establish this statement in Troy Lee's Lean formalization.

passages.quote: The construction first treats graph three-colourability. A colouring is interpolated from a finite grid to a polynomial. Two families of equations express that every vertex has one of three permitted colours and adjacent vertices have different colours. A polynomial vanishing on the whole grid has a certificate built from the grid's coordinate vanishing polynomials. A verifier can therefore test a colouring through its low-degree encoding and these vanishing certificates.

passages.section: Correcting an outer value at a prescribed point
passages.quote: Fix a target $a\in F^k$. A point oracle $f$ has degree-one labels, and an auxiliary table is supplied for each line through $a$. Choose a uniform direction $v\in F^k$, a nonzero uniform parameter $z\in F^\times$, a uniform homogeneous label $L$, an inner correction direction, and an independent inner-test seed. Run the inner test on the line's auxiliary row. If it fails, reject. Otherwise correct that row at $\Phi(z)$ and compare with $f(a+zv,L)$. If the comparison fails, reject. If both checks pass, return the correction at $\Phi(0)$, with the same inner correction direction and label.

passages.section: From finite samples to fair random bits
passages.quote: Some mathematical correctors use uniformly distributed nonzero field parameters. Sampling uniformly from $F^{\times}$ with a fixed fair-bit budget is inconvenient because $Q-1$ is not a power of two. The implemented verifier instead samples all four such parameters from the whole field. If any is zero, it accepts immediately and makes no queries. Otherwise it runs the seven-check verifier.

passages.section: The polynomial-time implementation
passages.quote: The information-theoretic verifier must be implemented by a polynomial-time machine; a bounded number of oracle queries alone does not provide this. The formal implementation computes the parameters, field arithmetic, seed codecs, query addresses and verdict in a fixed program language and compiles that language to Mathlib's `FinTM2` machine model.

passages.section: From every NP verifier to a graph
passages.quote: To make the tableau a bounded-arity constraint system, use a finite alphabet fixed by the source machine. Each row has one control-and-prefix variable and one optional-symbol variable for each stack position below $S(n)$. Let $w_0$ be the machine's fixed window size. Link constraints identify the stored prefix with the first $w_0$ cells of every stack.

passages.section: From every NP verifier to a graph
passages.quote: A constraint over an alphabet of size $A$ is converted to Boolean constraints by one-hot coding. Each source variable receives $A$ bits, exactly one of which is true; its true index is the encoded symbol. Validity constraints enforce this condition. A relation inspects the relevant one-hot blocks and accepts precisely the tuples accepted by the original finite relation. The alphabet size and local arity are constants fixed by the original machine. [The finite-domain encoding][lean-one-hot] proves that decoding a satisfying one-hot assignment and encoding a source assignment preserve all constraints.

passages.section: From every NP verifier to a graph
passages.quote: There is an executable version of this reduction, not just a polynomial bound on an existentially chosen graph. The program computes $T(n)$, $S(n)$ and the fixed source dimensions, enumerates the tableau variables and relations using arithmetic sum/product indices, emits the fixed-arity clauses and gadgets, and writes the graph's bitstring. The fixed finite alphabet and fixed relation arity make truth-table enumeration constant work per relation up to the machine-dependent factor $2^{k_0}$. Matrix emission is polynomial in the already bounded vertex count.

passages.section: Source and verification account
passages.quote: The fixed formal source is revision a0ce13ed0fa264f051c1278e039596ce65557fa4 of Lee's repository. The primary paper is the corrected [arXiv v2 of *A Simple Algebraic Proof of the PCP Theorem*][intro-paper], dated 22 October 2026. That public revision corrects the short low-degree test and acknowledges Lee's identification of an earlier mistake. A separate final SOSA proceedings edition has not been established identical to v2. Nor are the paper and Lean development asserted to be textually or parametrically identical: the chapters state the formalization's exact tests, constants and resource guarantees where these differ. Public links identify the supporting statements at the fixed revision. Source inspection, ordinary mathematical derivation, and finite illustrative calculations are distinguished from a fresh kernel-check receipt; this account does not by itself claim the latter.
